text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] probe-timeout-wave: EU-Canary 3 failures in 5m; threshold 3
sam: got the PD page, on it
pagerduty-bot: New incident created: <https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-78324|PD-78324> — page to SRE-EU rotation
elena: checking dashboards... saw timeout spikes across eu-west-1 probes starting 03:12 UTC
matt: logs show 504 from probe targets, connection reset messages from prober
diego: I'm current on-call, taking lead. starting runbook "synth-probe-timeout" now
nora: any customer impact yet? support reported 2 customers complaining about slow responses 03:15 UTC
elena: telemetry: frontend request latency for text-gen rose ~200ms for the same period, error-rate not elevated, looks like probe-specific
sam: paste of probe curl: ```curl -v https://probe-eu.redwood.prod/health-check -H 'X-Probe: canary'
* Connected to ...
< HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
``` 
matt: repro from prober box: netstat shows many TIME_WAIT to model-hosts; dns lookup ok
diego: scaling pods didn't help, suspect upstream NLB health checks flapping; checking NLB/ENI metrics
incident-bot: PD escalation: incident PD-78324 escalated to level2 after 10m without ack
elena: ack on PD, I'm in the page channel
sam: can we temporarily route canary probes to fallback region? we have config: ```prober.route = eu-west-1, fallback=eu-central-1```
diego: good idea; I'll update route policy to include fallback, apply in 2m
matt: FYI adding fallback will avoid more pages but doesn't fix upstream. still need postmortem
diego: applied change `prober.policy` -> `prefer: primary, fallback: eu-central-1, failover-threshold: 2m` — rolling restart prober workers
nora: support: told affected customers "we're investigating probe timeouts; no model-serving degradation detected", keeping them posted
sam: PD note: manual action taken to reduce pages: rerouted probes to fallback region — manual mitigation
incident-bot: PD-78324 status: acknowledged by elena at 03:28 UTC
matt: after reroute, probe failures dropped to 0 in 5m window
elena: creating an incident page in ops-docs, adding timeline + graphs
diego: root cause hypothesis: intermittent NLB connection limit hit in eu-west causing probe connections to reset; need to verify with cloud logs and LB metrics
sam: adding ticket to infra: increase NLB connection limits and add steady-state to autoscaling for prober targets
nora: decide if customer-facing postmortem needed? impact limited, but a few customers saw UI slowdowns. Recommend a short incident banner
elena: agree. I'll draft banner and link ops postmortem. Also scheduling follow-up with infra team to validate NLB config
matt: runbook item: add probe fanout smoothing to avoid thundering on NLB when prober restarts
diego: handing off active ownership to elena for post-incident, I'm off-call in 20m
elena: taking ownership — will post status here and update PD when postmortem ready
sam: one more: add alert suppression when we detect mass failover to fallback to avoid repeated PD pages
incident-bot: PD-78324 resolved by elena at 04:10 UTC — notes: reroute applied, monitoring stable, follow-ups scheduled
nora: thanks team. filing customer comms draft in #support-drafts
diego: thanks all, good quick mitigation :thumbsup:
elena: closing notes: follow-ups: infra ticket INFRA-1298 (NLB limits), SRE-234 (probe smoothing), customer banner draft submitted
matt: logs/metrics snapshot retained in incident folder: s3://redwood-ops/incidents/PD-78324
elena: will schedule a 30m retrospective tomorrow 10:00 UTC, invite to follow
